title: This Week in Finance & Tech
body:
Meta is facing its largest penalty to date following a court ruling in New Mexico. The company has been ordered to pay $25 billion in relation to privacy practices dating back to the Cambridge Analytica scandal. This sum exceeds previous settlements, including an $18 billion deal in California.

In other major corporate news, Elon Musk has confirmed that Tesla and SpaceX are exploring a potential merger. Special committees have been established at both companies to evaluate the possibility of combining the two entities.

Meanwhile, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has secured a win in court. A US district judge dismissed a lawsuit filed by his sister, Ann Altman, after she declined to attend a court-ordered independent medical examination.

Turning to labor policy, Brazil has approved a constitutional amendment to reduce the maximum work week to 40 hours. This change effectively bans six-day work weeks and could impact up to 30 million workers across the country.

Finally, Airbnb is changing its checkout policy. Starting with reservations booked on or after November 20th, hosts are no longer permitted to require guests to complete time-consuming chores like taking out the trash or doing the dishes.
